rule.formula: global_slot = callee_result; return 1 in al iff callee_result == 0, else 0 in al, where callee_result = callee(input, 0, 0x576d920, 1) and global_slot is the u64 at 0x599a078
rule.formula_note: the window calls the callee with rdi = input (entry rdi, never reassigned), rsi = 0, rdx = the table at 0x576d920 (RIP-relative lea), rcx = 1; it then stores the full 64-bit callee result to the global slot at 0x599a078 unconditionally, and returns sete on the full-rax zero test, so the verdict is 1 exactly when the callee result is zero. The rule is stated over al because sete sets only the low byte, but the zero test itself is on the full rax (test rax, rax), unlike the low-byte-only verdicts of the helper low-byte equality and u32 second-field equality windows. The neighboring 12-byte window at 0x54d5f20 (endbr64; mov rax, [0x599a078]; ret) reads exactly this slot, which supports reading the slot as a cache the window refreshes; that getter window is context only and is not claimed here.
rule.inputs: input (pointer in rdi, passed to the callee unchanged), callee_result (u64 rax from the call to 0x54d5f30), table_base (0x576d920, RIP-relative lea argument in rdx), global_slot (u64 at 0x599a078, written by the window)
